topic.subject: physics
topic.title: Magnets, fields and domain theory
topic.scopeBasis: TGS 2025-26: Domain Theory of Magnetism and magnets; TGS 2026-27: Electromagnetism
topic.overview: Magnets exert non-contact forces through fields. Domain theory connects the large-scale behaviour of magnetic materials to alignment inside the material.
learningGoals: Recall the precise Year 8 scientific vocabulary and symbols.
Apply the idea to an unfamiliar example rather than relying on recognition.
Use the command word, show working where needed and include every mark point.
mustMemoriseRules: Every bar magnet has north and south poles; like poles repel and unlike poles attract.
Iron, nickel and cobalt are magnetic; steel is magnetic because it contains iron.
A magnetic field is a region where a magnetic material or pole experiences a force.
Outside a magnet, field direction is conventionally from north to south.
Closer field lines represent a stronger field; field lines do not cross.
A plotting compass points along the local field direction.
In an unmagnetised ferromagnetic material, domains are arranged in many directions; magnetisation aligns more domains.
Heating, hammering or an alternating field can disorder domains and demagnetise a material.

mustMemoriseVocabulary.meaning: region near a magnet's end where its effect is strongest
region in which a magnetic force can act
model line showing field direction and relative strength
small compass used to map field direction
strongly attracted and able to be magnetised, such as iron
small region in which magnetic effects are aligned
make a material magnetic by increasing domain alignment
reduce magnetism by disturbing domain alignment

workedExamples.prompt: Which way does a compass north end point outside a bar magnet?
workedExamples.answer: Along the field line, from the magnet's north pole towards its south pole.

workedExamples.prompt: Why is a steel paper clip attracted before it becomes permanently magnetised?
workedExamples.answer: The magnet causes domains in the clip to align temporarily, producing attraction.

practicals.title: Map a bar magnet's field
practicals.aim: Plot field direction and shape around a magnet.
practicals.variables: IV: compass position; DV: compass direction; controls: magnet position/orientation and nearby magnetic objects.
practicals.method: Place a magnet beneath paper, move a plotting compass point by point, mark the north-end direction and join smooth lines with arrows.
practicals.expectedResult: Lines curve from north to south outside the magnet and are closest near poles.
practicals.safety: Keep magnets away from devices and anyone with relevant medical implants; avoid trapping fingers with strong magnets.
practicals.evaluation: Use many close points, keep the magnet fixed and remove steel objects that distort the field.

commonMistakes: Saying unmagnetised iron has no domains.
examTips: For poles: like repel, unlike attract.
Put arrows N to S outside the bar magnet.
Domains exist before magnetisation; alignment changes.
beforeStartingPractice: Read the key rules once, cover them, then retrieve them aloud or in writing.
Use MC first for confidence, but finish with typed, calculation, practical or explanation evidence.
After an error, study the explanation; the same concept returns later in a different format and again after 2 and 7 days.

practicals.subject: physics
practicals.title: Map a bar magnet's field
practicals.aim: Plot field direction and shape around a magnet.
practicals.variables: IV: compass position; DV: compass direction; controls: magnet position/orientation and nearby magnetic objects.
practicals.method: Place a magnet beneath paper, move a plotting compass point by point, mark the north-end direction and join smooth lines with arrows.
practicals.expectedResult: Lines curve from north to south outside the magnet and are closest near poles.
practicals.safety: Keep magnets away from devices and anyone with relevant medical implants; avoid trapping fingers with strong magnets.
practicals.evaluation: Use many close points, keep the magnet fixed and remove steel objects that distort the field.
